description: Na₄MgTi₂(GeO₅)₂ crystallizes in the tetragonal P̅4m2 space group. Na is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to four O atoms. There are two shorter (2.24 Å) and two longer (2.33 Å) Na-O bond lengths. Mg is bonded to four equivalent O atoms to form MgO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four equivalent TiO₅ trigonal bipyramids and edges with two equivalent GeO₄ tetrahedra. All Mg-O bond lengths are 2.01 Å. Ti is bonded to five O atoms to form distorted TiO₅ trigonal bipyramids that share corners with two equivalent MgO₄ tetrahedra and corners with four GeO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Ti-O bond distances ranging from 1.72-2.05 Å. There are two inequivalent Ge sites. In the first Ge site, Ge is bonded to four equivalent O atoms to form distorted GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four equivalent TiO₅ trigonal bipyramids and edges with two equivalent MgO₄ tetrahedra. All Ge-O bond lengths are 2.20 Å. In the second Ge site, Ge is bonded to four equivalent O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four equivalent TiO₅ trigonal bipyramids. All Ge-O bond lengths are 1.78 Å. There are three inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to two equivalent Na, one Ti, and one Ge atom. In the second O site, O is bonded to two equivalent Na, one Mg, one Ti, and one Ge atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing ONa₂MgTiGe trigonal bipyramids. In the third O site, O is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one Ti atom.
